title: Logging: peer error bodies, cause chains, per-request spans, consistent levels
description:
mimid-server's logs are too thin to debug interop. Found 2026-11-13 before the IETF 127 table with Haven:

1. PeerError::Rejected keeps only the status (peer.rs:386-392). The peer's response body, e.g. Haven's UpdateRoomResponse with responseCode and errorDescription, is dropped, so the log says only 'peer provider failed: peer answered 400'.
2. Disposition events print errors with %error (http.rs:242, 345, 359, 386, 390), which shows the top message only. A reqwest or TLS failure loses its cause.
3. No per-request event or span. Inbound requests log nothing unless they fail; PeerClient's outbound calls log nothing at all.
4. Most hub refusals (MLS validation, policy, epoch, GroupInfo mismatch) are debug-only, and some levels don't match their meaning (for example warn on correctly refused peer input, warn on a failed local operation).

Mark wants lots of logging, done the idiomatic Rust way: the tracing facility already in use, native structured fields, one disposition event per failure, source chains kept and not repeated, and bounded volume. The stopgap for the weekend is on the hackathon EC2 (RUST_LOG debug for mimid crates, and a socat -v -x wire capture of the Haven :8443 proxy); see mimid-1wgh.46.3.
design:
PLAN (draft 2026-11-13, awaiting Mark's approval). Follows the logging and error-handling-in-rust skills and AGENTS.md 'Secrets never reach logs'.

A. Peer rejection keeps evidence (peer.rs)
- PeerError::Rejected gains the response body, read with the existing MAX_BODY_LEN cap and then truncated to a small preview bound (proposal: 4 KiB) plus the full length. Display stays 'peer answered {status}' (no body in Display). Debug may show the body.
- Where an endpoint defines a typed error response (UpdateRoomResponse and similar), decode it best-effort into a structured field (responseCode, errorDescription). A body that won't decode stays as bytes.
- Callers that match Rejected keep working (status and retry_after unchanged).

B. One disposition event per failure, with its cause chain (http.rs and main.rs)
- Record errors as error = &error as &dyn std::error::Error, not %error, so tracing-subscriber records the source chain.
- Audit the Display texts on the affected error types so none repeats its #[source] (error-handling rule).
- Peer rejections get fields peer, endpoint, status, response_len and the decoded responseCode/errorDescription if present. The body preview goes at debug only, escaped and bounded: never request or response bodies at INFO.
- Levels by meaning, at the layer that owns disposition. A local operation that failed (peer down, 5xx): error. Peer input mimid correctly refused: debug (or info if it has admin value), never warn or error. Abnormal-but-served: warn. PeerClient itself only propagates, so it emits debug-level events at most.

C. Spans and per-request events
- tower-http TraceLayer on the axum router: one span per request with method, matched route (template, not raw path), status and latency, recorded at debug. Turn off its on_failure logging so it doesn't duplicate B's disposition events.
- #[tracing::instrument(skip_all, fields(room_id, endpoint, peer))] on the hub and follower handlers and the PeerClient methods, so every nested event carries context. Never put a body in a span field.
- PeerClient emits one debug event per completed call: peer, endpoint, status, elapsed, request_len and response_len.
- Field keys reuse the existing ones (room_id, endpoint, user, current_epoch, reason, index, error, denied) and add peer, status, elapsed, request_len and response_len.

D. Output and policy
- Optional JSON output (tracing-subscriber json feature), chosen by an env var such as MIMID_LOG_FORMAT=json, for jq during interop. The default stays the current human format.
- DECISION FOR MARK: event-identity policy. Either name every info, warn and error event (tracing name: "...") because interop logs get grepped and queried, or leave all events unnamed as local human diagnostics. Recommendation: named.

E. Tests
- A capture-subscriber test asserting that a peer 4xx produces one disposition event carrying status, the decoded errorDescription and the error source chain, and no second event for the same failure.
- Extend the secrets canary to the new span fields and the body preview.
- Volume check: a flood of refused requests produces only debug events, so production at RUST_LOG=info stays quiet.

Out of scope: metrics (no facility yet), and the agent crate.
notes: 2026-11-13: Mark approved the plan. DECISION: named events (every info/warn/error event gets a stable tracing name). Build it.
